_note: How each core lays out real-time-clock state. Unlike the other files here this one is NOT
synced from the registry pages: the specifications do not describe clock layouts. These come
from files real cores wrote, or the core's own source where no file has been sampled, cross-checked
against one-saves-convert's rtc module. A core absent from this file records no clock convention,
which is also what a core gets whose source is unpublished and whose files nobody has sampled.
Layouts: appended | packed | sidecar. A footer (appended or packed) states timestamp_width, the
bytes its host clock takes; a sidecar has none. Which chip the state belongs to is the save's own
business: mostly the system, but the MiSTer Game Boy cores also keep a HuC-3 in the same footer,
packed differently, so for those it is the cartridge type.
Each entry's `evidence` says where its facts were read: a file, or the source at a commit.
